title: Interval
preamble:
# Interval

The `Interval` type. An `Interval` is a
half-open `[start, end)` range over either two `Time` values or
two `Date` values; the operand type determines the interval
type.

Paired with:
- [LTIM] for the `Time`, `Date`, and `Duration`
  types and their semantics.
- [LSTR] for the JSON wire-format conventions.
- [LEXP] for the broader expression
  surface (`in`, `overlaps`, `contains`, `..`).

## What this is not

- Not a general range type over integers or floats. `Interval`
  is `Time`-or-`Date` only. Numeric ranges remain expressed by
  comparison.
- Not a closed-interval type. `start .. end` always means
  `[start, end)`. Authors who need the closed form add `1us`
  (Time) or `1_d` (Date).
- Not a set-operations library. Union, intersection, and
  difference on intervals are deferred per [LINT.10.3].
